loading: Waiting for it to show up on screen…
waitDefault: The step counts once you do it

confirm.title: Stop the tour?
confirm.body: Your progress stays in the checklist on «My tasks». You can continue from there or from «Help → Get started».

missing.title: Can’t see where to point
missing.body: The element isn’t on screen — maybe it’s on another page or still loading. If it never shows up, the step can be skipped.

workspaces.title: Spaces
workspaces.body: On the left is the rail of spaces: each has its own projects, members and tags. A new one is created here too, but let’s start where you are.

tree-add.title: Projects on the left
tree-add.body: Projects live in the tree. Press «+» above it and choose «Project».
tree-add.wait: Counts once the project form opens

project-create.title: Name the project
project-create.body: The name also sets the address: /project/name. The address is set once — if it matters, type it yourself.
project-create.wait: Type a name and press ↵ — the step counts once the project appears in the tree

board-add.title: Add a board
board-add.body: Tasks live on boards. Press «+» next to the project, type a name and press Enter — the board opens with four columns.

task-create.title: Create a task
task-create.body: The «Create task» row at the foot of «{todo}» stays visible during this step. Type a title and press Enter.
task-create.wait: Click the row or press C — counts once the card appears

card-fields.title: Right on the card
card-fields.body: Priority, due date, tags and assignees are edited without opening the task — click the icon on the card.

dnd-card.title: Drag the card
dnd-card.body: A task’s status changes by moving it between columns. Drag the card to «{inProgress}» — with the mouse or the keyboard.
dnd-card.wait: Counts once the card is in another column

card-open.title: Open the task
card-open.body: Click the card or press ↵ on the selected one — the task window opens with all its fields.
card-open.wait: Counts once the task window opens

tm-close.title: Everything saves itself
tm-close.body: There’s no «Save» button — fields save at once. Close the window: the changes are already on the card.
tm-close.wait: Counts once the window closes — by the button, Esc or a click outside

done.title: Basics done
done.body: Next come the optional chapters: in the checklist on «My tasks» and in «Help → Get started».

task-open.title: Open a task
task-open.body: This chapter walks the task window. Open any card on the board.
task-open.wait: Counts once the task window opens

tm-due.title: Due date and repeat
tm-due.body: Set a due date — repeat and reminder are set up in the same calendar.
tm-due.wait: Counts once the task has a due date

tm-assignees.title: Assignees
tm-assignees.body: Choose who works on the task — there can be several.
tm-assignees.wait: Counts once the task has an assignee

tm-priority.title: Priority
tm-priority.body: Priority colours the card’s stripe, and the board can sort by it.
tm-priority.wait: Counts once a priority is set

tm-tags.title: Tags
tm-tags.body: A tag is created right here. The board can lay itself out in columns by tags — the main way to arrange tasks your way.
tm-tags.wait: Counts once the task has a tag

tm-description.title: Description
tm-description.body: Markdown, attachments and mentions with {'@'}. Saved when you leave the field.
tm-description.wait: Counts once the description is saved

tm-tabs.title: Subtasks, activity, links
tm-tabs.body: Below the description are subtasks and the feed: comments mixed with the history of changes. Links to other tasks are in the properties panel.

inbox-open.title: One feed for notes and reminders
inbox-open.body: «Inbox» opens from the button in the top bar or with G I, and doesn’t cover the board.

inbox-feed.title: What’s in the feed
inbox-feed.body: Fired reminders on top, then today, later and notes. ↑↓ walk the records, 1–4 are filters.

inbox-capture.title: Write a thought down
inbox-capture.body: «Record» or N M from anywhere. One line: with a time it’s a reminder, without — a note.
inbox-capture.wait: Counts once the record appears in the feed

inbox-actions.title: Sort a record out
inbox-actions.body: A record has its own keys: E — done, H — snooze, T — turn into a task. The rest is in the record’s menu.

inbox-done.title: Inbox always at hand
inbox-done.body: The number on the button counts fired reminders. Today’s summary of the feed is on «My tasks».

stage-select.title: The stage, right on the board
stage-select.body: This is where you choose what the board shows: a sprint, the backlog or all tasks. Key ⇧E.

stage-strip.title: The stage strip
stage-strip.body: When the board shows a stage, its goals and progress sit above the columns. ⇧H folds the strip to a line, and the board remembers.

stage-page.title: The stage page
stage-page.body: The strip’s menu leads to the stage page — scope, burn-up and closing the stage. From the board — G E.

stage-nav.title: All stages
stage-nav.body: Stages of every project in the space are in «Stages» on the left.

keys-palette.title: Everything from the keyboard
keys-palette.body: The ⌘K palette finds tasks, boards and people and runs commands. Open it with a click or ⌘K.

keys-palette-tab.title: Actions on a task
keys-palette-tab.body: Pick a task and press Tab — its actions appear: status, due date, assignee. Esc closes the palette.

keys-sheet.title: The cheat sheet
keys-sheet.body: Every key is in the cheat sheet. Open it with the «Keys» button or the ? key.
keys-sheet.wait: Counts once the cheat sheet opens

keys-sheet-read.title: Keys by section
keys-sheet-read.body: The board, a card, the task window, «Inbox» — each has its own keys. Esc closes the cheat sheet.

keys-card.title: Cards by arrows
keys-card.body: On a board the arrows select a card, ↵ opens it, E completes it, P and a digit set the priority.

tags-group.title: Columns by tags
tags-group.body: A board can be laid out by tags instead of statuses: each column is a tag. Switch it here.

tags-columns.title: A task in several columns
tags-columns.body: A task with two tags stands in two columns, and moving it between columns changes its tag.

tags-window.title: Project tags
tags-window.body: Tags, their prefixes and merging are in the «Project» window, on the «Tags» tab. It opens from here or with ⌘,.

group-add.title: Project groups
group-add.body: When there are many projects, they go into groups. Press «+» above the tree and choose «Group».
group-add.wait: Counts once the group appears in the tree

dnd-project.title: Drag a project into the group
dnd-project.body: The tree drags just like a board: take a project and drop it into the group.
dnd-project.wait: Counts once the project is in the group

project-window.title: The «Project» window
project-window.body: A project’s tags, stages, estimation and address are in the «Project» window: the project’s menu, or ⌘, on its board.

gitlab-board.title: GitLab on the board
gitlab-board.body: Connections, rules and the sync journal are in the GitLab window from the board’s menu.

gitlab-card.title: Tasks from GitLab
gitlab-card.body: Cards from GitLab carry the issue number. Edits go back to GitLab, and conflicts are sorted out in a window of their own.

welcome-mine.title: Welcome to the team
welcome-mine.body: You were invited into a space where projects and boards already exist — there’s nothing to create. Let’s start with «My tasks»: everything assigned to you, from every board.

welcome-board.title: The team’s boards
welcome-board.body: Projects and boards are in the tree on the left. Open any board to see the team’s tasks.

welcome-inbox.title: Inbox
welcome-inbox.body: Notes and reminders in one feed. Opens from the button or with G I.

welcome-search.title: Search and ⌘K
welcome-search.body: Find a task, a board or a person and run a command — from the ⌘K palette.

welcome-done.title: Done
welcome-done.body: «Basics» and the optional chapters stay in the checklist on «My tasks» and in «Help → Get started».

m-nav.title: Navigation
m-nav.body: At the bottom are five tabs: «My tasks», «Board», «Inbox», «Search» and «More».

m-board.title: Boards
m-board.body: «Board» opens your last board. Columns swipe sideways; the project tree slides out with a swipe from the left edge.

m-fab.title: The «+» button
m-fab.body: A new task, reminder or note — from any screen.

m-inbox.title: Inbox
m-inbox.body: Notes and reminders in one feed. Swipe a record — done or snooze.

m-search.title: Search
m-search.body: Tasks, boards, people and commands — in one search.

m-done.title: The tour is in «More»
m-done.body: Settings and help are there too. You can take the tour again any time.

wc-inbox.title: Inbox
wc-inbox.body: Notes and reminders moved here from their own sections — everything is in place. Open the feed — G I, write a thought down — N M.

wc-capture.title: Capture in one line
wc-capture.body: «+» → record: with a time it’s a reminder, without — a note. From the keyboard — N M or N R.

wc-stage.title: The stage, right on the board
wc-stage.body: A sprint, the backlog or all tasks — chosen here or with ⇧E. Above the columns is the stage strip with its goals.

wc-view.title: Board view and saved views
wc-view.body: The sliders button opens a panel on the right: cards, fields and saved views. ⇧V.

wc-project.title: The «Project» window
wc-project.body: A project’s tags, stages and estimation are in one window: ⌘, on the board or the project’s menu.

wc-palette.title: Everything from the keyboard
wc-palette.body: Search, commands and actions on a task (Tab) — in one ⌘K palette. Every key is in the «?» cheat sheet.

stages.select: Pick a stage on the board

projects.move: Move a project into a group

checklist.title: Get started
checklist.doneBody: Basics and {n} chapter of {of}. | Basics and {n} chapters of {of}.
checklist.doneLocked: The «GitLab» chapter opens once a GitLab project is connected to a board.
